title: Serverless Federated AUPRC Optimization for Multi-Party Collaborative Imbalanced Data Mining

problem.claim: Multi-party collaborative training must support imbalanced data mining tasks where accuracy-oriented classifiers can be biased toward the primary class.

gap.claim: Although single-machine methods exist for AUPRC maximization, multi-party collaborative training algorithms for this objective had not been studied, and existing methods were not applicable to large-scale settings because they depend on each local data point.

narrative_sequence.summary: Serverless multi-party collaborative training has attracted attention because avoiding a server node bottleneck can reduce communication cost.
Traditional serverless collaborative training algorithms were designed mainly for balanced tasks and accuracy optimization.
Skewed real-world data can cause accuracy-trained classifiers to become biased toward the primary class, motivating AUPRC as an effective metric.
AUPRC maximization had been studied on single machines but not for multi-party collaborative training, which introduces critical challenges.
Single-machine AUPRC methods maintain an inner state for each local data point, making them unsuitable for large-scale multi-party training.

source_observation.claim: Accuracy-oriented training can perform poorly on imbalanced data because models may become biased toward the primary class.

interpretation.claim: Evaluation objectives should reflect class imbalance when the primary class dominates the data.

application.claim: Consider precision-recall-based objectives such as AUPRC for imbalanced classification tasks.

exception.claim: The supplied units do not establish that AUPRC is appropriate for every classification setting.

source_observation.claim: Methods that maintain state for every local data point may not scale to large-scale multi-party collaborative training.

interpretation.claim: Distributed algorithm design must account for per-party data-state dependencies and communication or storage constraints.

application.claim: When adapting single-machine methods to collaborative settings, examine whether local per-example state remains feasible.

exception.claim: The supplied units do not quantify the scalability threshold or establish that per-example state is always infeasible.
